title: cvENGINE Sentinel result contract
description: Both halves of the exchange between cvENGINE and a Sentinel. $defs/targets is what the server hands a Sentinel for each task kind (the task's target); $defs/results is what a Sentinel sends to POST /api/v1/sentinel/tasks/{id}/result; $defs/partials is what a streamed kind (bbot_discovery) sends to POST /api/v1/sentinel/tasks/{id}/partial while it runs, before the result that closes it. The server clips and validates every result anyway (agentapi.sentinel_broker.clean_result); this file is what a correct client keeps to, so the server never has to. Bounds are asserted equal to the server's own limits, and every target the server builds is validated against it, by tests/test_sentinel_contract.py. Bump contract_version (and say so in CHANGELOG) for any change a client must follow.

cve_ids.description: Optional: the CVE ids the template names (nuclei's classification.cve-id). Only well-formed ids are kept; a result without the field is stored without it.

type.description: Optional (1.3.5): nuclei's protocol type of the template (its "type" field). The server keeps it, lowercased, when it is one of http, tcp, network, javascript, dns, ssl, headless, file, whois, code or websocket, and drops any other value.

request.description: Optional (1.3.5): the request the template sent when it matched. The server keeps the first 4096 characters, control bytes but not newlines removed.

response.description: Optional (1.3.5): the answer that matched. The server keeps the first 4096 characters, control bytes but not newlines removed.

report.description: the raw WPScan JSON report; at most 8 MiB serialised

the raw JSON report of the thorough WordPress scan (one site, plugins and themes in mixed detection mode); at most 8 MiB serialised, partial when the run was cut at its time limit (exit code 4 and a scan_aborted text)

manufacturer.description: informational: cvENGINE stores the product, as a local wafw00f run does, not who makes it

generic.description: something blocked the probes but wafw00f could name no product

partials.description: the seq of the last batch sent: the server refuses a final result before it has every batch

mode.description: the mode the run finished in (a run that ran out of memory is retried one step lighter)

incomplete.description: bbot stopped part way (a crash or the time limit) after it had found something; empty for a whole run

problems.description: modules bbot skipped at start-up (a rejected or missing key)

hard_failures.description: modules whose set-up failed (gowitness without a working browser)

evidence.description: what the probe read (signals, the library record); at most 16 KB as JSON

touched.description: every host a request was sent to

refused.description: every host a hop (a redirect, a script) was refused for by the scope policy

resolved.description: every address each name answered, as answered: the server judges them

errors.description: a lookup the resolver could not answer (never a name without an address)

objects.description: raw names from the first listing page; the server redacts them before anything is stored or shown

evidence.description: what the finding rests on; the server clips it before anything is stored

resolvable.description: category -> check-name prefixes this run could decide (what it no longer finds resolves)

own.description: the name's own site as the scanner asked it, when the task gave none

page.description: what the distinct application's own page states (the server reads versions from it); only for a name the scanner judged distinct

secret.description: the value itself, over the authenticated channel only: the server fingerprints and masks it and never stores it

validation.description: Kingfisher's validation.outcome only: its response is never sent

sources_content.description: a source map that embeds the original sources (sourcesContent)

xml.description: the raw nmap -oX report; cvENGINE reads it with the same hardened parser as a local run
the raw nmap -oX report; cvENGINE reads it with the same hardened parser as a local run

vulnerable.description: null: the detector could not decide (inconclusive)

painted.description: false: the server painted nothing before the wait ran out

image.description: the pre-authentication screen as a PNG of at most 4 MiB; the reading of it stays on the server

open.description: true: the one credential-less attempt was let through; null: this Sentinel has no client for the database

plain.description: the plain SYN drew a reset

odd.description: the FIN+PSH+URG segment drew a reset; null when it was not sent

valid.description: mode validate: nuclei -validate accepted the template

fixture_ok.description: mode validate: the template did not match a benign loopback fixture; null when not run

outcomes.description: mode test: one per target, in order

hit.description: the first nuclei result line of the host, its request and response cut to 8000 characters

found.description: a TLS service answered: its certificate is in cert; false with no error means nothing there speaks TLS

error.description: the endpoint was not asked or could not be probed: unknown, not "nothing there"

evidence.description: JSON data the check kept as its evidence; the server bounds its size

state.description: unknown: no usable answer, the server keeps the finding as baddns rated it

id.description: the route's URL, as the task named it

evidence.description: markers, bytes, cookie names, the headers kept, fingerprints, the front page's scripts and the libraries their files state; never the body; at most 128 KB as JSON

sensitive.description: per kind of sensitive data: its count and one masked sample

value.description: the value itself, over the authenticated channel only: the server fingerprints and masks it for its secrets inventory and never stores it

error.description: the route could not be asked: it carries no state, and the server reads it as unknown

etags.description: tags the run must always exclude (dos)
tags the run must always exclude (dos)
tags the run must always exclude (dos)

token.description: the project's WPScan API token, for this one run; the server replaces it with *** once the task ends
the project's WPScan API token, for this one run; the server replaces it with *** once the task ends

timeout_seconds.description: the whole scan of this one site, in seconds (hours): the client ends it 30 seconds before and reports what it read; the server keeps the task's lease alive for this long plus a grace to report, and no longer

strict_scope.description: bbot's --strict-scope: the target's subdomains are not in scope either

timeout_seconds.description: the whole run, lighter retries included

api_keys.description: the project has API keys for bbot modules. They are never in the target: only the built-in scanner is offered such a task, and it reads them once through POST /api/v1/sentinel/tasks/{id}/secret

trufflehog.description: bbot's trufflehog module may run (it verifies a found secret against its issuer); never for a bug bounty project

allowed.description: the names a redirect may lead to (the host's apex and www)

name.description: the bucket, or the Azure storage account

read_object.description: a public listing may be followed by one HEAD of a listed object (default true)

rate.description: requests per second within the task (the server keeps the global rate)

host.description: the name the address used to serve: the Host header and TLS server name of an http(s) check

ip.description: the last known address, asked as itself

scheme.description: http(s): a GET of / as host, any answer counts; tcp: a connect, nothing sent

gap.description: seconds between any two requests of the task

host_gap.description: seconds between two requests to one name

max_requests.description: the requests the task may make in all (a certificate read counts as three); a name that does not fit is reported partial

own.description: the name's own front page as the server last stored it: asked here only when absent

gap.description: seconds between two requests within the task (the server keeps the global pace)

connect_ip.description: ask this address with the name as the Host header (a virtual host)

root.description: the host's stored front page: the second baseline

leads.description: mount directories the host's crawled and archived URLs show, most often seen first; the scanner adds those of robots.txt and sitemap.xml

gap.description: seconds between two requests within the task (the server keeps the global pace)

secrets_scan.description: A batch of web hosts whose pages and own scripts the Sentinel fetches (bounded, anonymous, same origin) and scans with Kingfisher, detection only (--no-validate) unless validate is true. validate is only ever true in a task for the built-in scanner, for a project that opted in (cveFeed.secrets_validation): the second Kingfisher pass then loads validate_rules only, and only when the scanner's Kingfisher is validate_kingfisher. rules_bundle_sha256 names the instance's custom rules (GET /api/v1/sentinel/secret-rules/bundle), null when there are none.

names.description: the only hosts any fetch may reach: the batch's own

nmap_full.description: one address: every TCP port, open ports only

nmap_verify.description: nmap service detection (and safe NSE scripts) on named ports of one address

scripts.description: NSE scripts by name; a Sentinel runs only the names on its own reviewed list

path_probe.description: closed TCP ports of hosts the scans reach: the built-in scanner measures whether its own path loses a malformed probe

nuclei_validate.description: an AI-written or approved nuclei template: validate (syntax and a benign loopback fixture) or test (against the targets)

template.description: the template text: a new AI-written one (at most 20,000 bytes) or an installed, approved one (at most 200,000)

always.description: reviewed whatever its records; any other name only when it has an MX record of its own and is not a CNAME

confirm_resolvers.description: resolvers also asked whether a record is missing (CVENGINE_HYGIENE_CONFIRM_RESOLVERS)

rdap.description: ask a registry whether a domain an SPF include or DMARC report address names is registered (default true)

triggers.description: the names baddns reported (its Trigger), lower case

providers.description: cvENGINE's takeover provider lists (cveFeed/data/takeover_providers.json), the one copy

patterns.description: regular expressions, matched case insensitively from the start of a name server name

urls.description: the host's routes, asked one after another: each on that host, http or https

scope_policy.description: What a scanner may touch, carried in the task and enforced by the scanner on every hop, on top of its own floor (never loopback, link-local, metadata or, unless it is internal, private space). The server applies the same rules again to everything it stores.

in_scope_domains.description: a name is in scope when it is one of these or under one, on a dot boundary

exact_host.description: the target was added as exactly one host: no name under it is in scope

deny_ranges.description: CIDR ranges never touched: the internal ranges the project declared (only a Sentinel inside them scans them, as targets of their own) and a bug bounty program's out-of-scope addresses

bounty.description: the project works a bug bounty program: no module that uses a found credential runs

bbot_discovery.description: One batch of what a running bbot discovery found since the last one, POSTed to /api/v1/sentinel/tasks/{id}/partial. seq starts at 1 and grows by one per batch; a batch the server already has (seq at or below the last one it took) is answered again as a duplicate and stored once. Every list is what bbot reported in scope since the previous batch.

scan_name.description: bbot's own name for the run

data.description: the image file, base64; at most 2 MiB before encoding

probe_scope.description: What a probe task may touch, computed by the server when it builds the task (exclusions, archived hosts, the targets' name scope, a bug bounty program's scope, the hosts a page may read scripts from, the private addresses the project authorised) and enforced by the scanner at every hop, redirects and script reads included, on top of its own floor. A name is allowed when it is in hosts or equal to or under a domain, and is not excluded; an address must also pass the floor, blocked and the private rule. Missing or malformed, it allows nothing.

private.description: the server allows private addresses (a lab install); an external Sentinel still never reaches them, and an internal one only with this

addresses.description: private addresses the project authorised (its own tailnet devices), reached only when asked for as themselves

blocked.description: CIDR ranges the server never scans
